chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram getting cupping done. He (peace be upon him) said: No, unless it is inevitable, so let him get cupping done, and the place of the cupping should not be shaved.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram get cupping done and shave the area?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while shaving the specific site of cupping is generally prohibited for the Muhrim, it becomes permissible if there is no alternative (bud), provided the cupping itself is performed. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'necessity permits the prohibited' (al-darurat tubih al-mahzurat), balancing ritual purity with practical medical needs during the sacred state of Ihram. The narration specifically limits the exception to the localized area rather than a general allowance for hair removal.
